topic: After a shoulder dislocation: the road back

slides.headline: Shoulder popped out? The road back
slides.sub: A realistic roadmap after a shoulder dislocation, from sling to sport.

slides.title: First, get it checked properly
slides.body: A dislocated shoulder needs medical care to confirm it's back in place and check nerves, blood supply and bone. Avoid trying to put it back in yourself or letting a mate try.

slides.title: The early weeks: calm and protect
slides.body: Your doctor may suggest a sling for a short time. Gentle elbow, wrist and hand movement, plus pain-guided shoulder exercises from your physio, usually start early.

slides.title: Middle stage: rebuild strength
slides.body: As things settle, the focus moves to rotator cuff and shoulder blade strength, then control in different positions. Progress is usually guided by how the shoulder responds, not the calendar.

slides.title: Late stage: back to sport and work
slides.body: Before contact sport, overhead work or the gym, you'll want strength, range and confidence in the positions that matter to you. Your physio can test this rather than guessing.

slides.title: When to get it looked at again
slides.body: Numbness or tingling in the arm, a shoulder that slips or feels unstable again, or pain that is getting worse rather than better are worth a prompt review.

slides.headline: Building back after a dislocation?
slides.body: Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios guide each stage, test your strength and help you return to the things you love.

caption:
A shoulder dislocation is a big moment. The road back is usually steady rather than quick.

First, it needs medical care to confirm it's back in place and nothing else is hurt. After that, rehab tends to move through stages: calming things down, rebuilding rotator cuff and shoulder blade strength, then getting ready for the positions your sport or work demands.

Most progress is guided by how your shoulder responds rather than a fixed date. Numbness, a shoulder that feels unstable again, or pain that keeps building are worth a prompt review.

story.body: It usually goes in stages: protect, rebuild strength, then return to sport. Progress follows your shoulder, not the calendar.
